outcome.answer:
Tool specifications can be used as the main source for synthetic test-case generation by extracting semantics from function names, natural-language descriptions, and typed parameter schemas, then using that information to synthesize scenarios without manual curation, examples, or live tool execution [1]. One paper does this from a single MCP specification by enriching raw schemas, generating graded scenarios with synthetic tool outputs, and expanding them into mock-data-grounded multi-turn dialogues, producing realistic evaluation scenarios for tool-using agents [1].

Related work broadens this idea into full synthetic environments: one framework has a teacher model create novel tasks and tool ecosystems, then uses a user simulator, mock tool system, and rubric-based rewards to support stable evaluation and training [2]. Another line focuses less on specifications themselves and more on stress-testing agents with simulated environments, dynamic hazards, or hard samples, such as recoverable tool unreliability and failure-driven hard trace generation [3,7].
